                    ### Question
                    An 15-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department after he passed out in the hallway. On presentation, he is alert but confused about why he is in the hospital. He says that he remembers seeing flashes of light to his right while walking out of class but cannot recall what happened next. His next memory is being woken up by emergency responders who wheeled him into an ambulance. A friend who was with him at the time says that he seemed to be swallowing repeatedly and staring out into space. He has never had an episode like this before, and his past medical history is unremarkable. Which of the following characteristics is most likely true of the cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options

opb. Demonstrates quick and repetitive jerks of extremities
opc. Episodes with 3-4 hertz spike and wave discharges
opd. Isolated to the left occipital lobe
ope. Starts in the left occipital lobe and then generalizes

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of confusion, loss of consciousness, and visual disturbances (flashes of light) suggest a seizure, likely originating from the occipital lobe. The presence of visual auras indicates focal seizure activity, which can start in the left occipital lobe and may generalize to other areas. This aligns with the consensus that seizures can begin focally and then generalize. Therefore, the most likely characteristic of the cause of this patient's symptoms is that it starts in the left occipital lobe and then generalizes.
